holidays.name: National Red Rose Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the classic red rose, the ultimate symbol of love and romance. Folks are encouraged to give, receive, or simply stop and smell a few red roses.
holidays.origin: Observed unofficially in the United States, this flower-themed day is part of a long tradition of floral celebrations tied to the rose's status as a symbol of love, and it is widely listed on June 12 in holiday calendars.
holidays.funFact: Fossils show roses have been around for about 35 million years, which means roses were blooming long before humans came up with Valentine's Day.

holidays.name: National Jerky Day
holidays.description: A salute to the chewy, salty, protein-packed snack that has fueled hikers, road-trippers, and gas station adventurers for generations. Flavors range from classic beef to teriyaki, peppered, and even exotic meats.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday popularized by snack lovers and food calendars. Jerky itself has ancient roots, with Indigenous peoples of the Andes making a dried meat called ch'arki.
holidays.funFact: The word 'jerky' comes from the Quechua word 'ch'arki,' meaning dried, salted meat.

holidays.name: Loving Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the 1967 Supreme Court decision Loving v. Virginia, which struck down laws banning interracial marriage in the United States. It's a day for celebrating love, diversity, and family.
holidays.origin: The ruling came on June 12, 1967, after Richard and Mildred Loving fought for the right to remain married in Virginia. The day has been celebrated as an informal observance since the late 1990s and gained momentum through grassroots events and festivals.
holidays.funFact: The couple's last name was Loving, which is perhaps the most perfectly named case in Supreme Court history.

holidays.name: World Day Against Child Labour
holidays.description: An international awareness day dedicated to highlighting the plight of child laborers and encouraging action to end child labour around the world.
holidays.origin: Launched by the International Labour Organization in 2002 to draw attention to the global extent of child labour and the efforts needed to eliminate it.
holidays.funFact: The ILO's campaign for the day brings together governments, workers' groups, and civil society, and the date was chosen to build year-round momentum for ending child labour.

holidays.name: Superman Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of the Man of Steel to dust off their capes and celebrate the iconic DC superhero with movie marathons, comic readings, and plenty of red-and-blue fashion.
holidays.origin: Superman Day is a fan-driven pop culture celebration. Superman debuted in Action Comics #1 in 1938, and the character has inspired countless adaptations in comics, film, TV, and animation.
holidays.funFact: Superman was created by writer Jerry Siegel and artist Joe Shuster, who sold the rights to the character for just $130.
